explanation_full: This table compares how well different machine learning models predict the target variable, which is Hydrogen Production Rate (HPR). The models tested include KNN, RF, XGBoost, SVM, and DT. The key metric here is R² (R-squared), which measures how much of the variation in the HPR is explained by the model; a value closer to 1 is better. KNN performed the best, achieving an R² of 0.8172, significantly outperforming the next best model, RF, which scored 0.7756. Furthermore, KNN had the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) at 0.1132, indicating the smallest average prediction error. In practical terms, choosing KNN suggests that it provides the most reliable and accurate prediction of HPR based on the available features, making it the preferred method for future predictions. However, users should remember that model performance is only as good as the data it is trained on, so the predictions should be used with caution and validated against real-world measurements.
